channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as minority leader for the next Congress
item.description: House Republicans on Tuesday elected Jim Jordan as minority leader for the next Congress, beating Majority Leader Steve Scalise, according to multiple sources.

item.title: 'Central role in ecosystem: If something happens to Nvidia, it's going to be a catastrophe'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Raphaëlle d’Ornano, Founder and Managing Partner of D’Ornano + Co. “Nvidia has an absolutely central role in the ecosystem,” she explains, “If something happens to Nvidia, it's going to be a catastrophe.” When the discussion turns to geopolitics, she warns, “there is a real war happening here. It's an economic war,” describing the competition for frontier AI capabilities as a struggle with profound economic, military, and societal implications. The resulting analysis reveals an industry characterized by extraordinary technological momentum, but increasingly shaped by concentrated corporate power, geopolitical confrontation, and political resistance to its physical infrastructure.

item.title: Anthropic eyes $1.4 trillion valuation in blockbuster IPO
item.description: US firm Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, has announced it will offer 825 million shares at a price between $70 and $78 apiece during its planned IPO. This will give the firm a valuation of around 1.4 trillion dollars. The blockbuster IPO will come at a time investors are becoming increasingly concerned about risks associated with the AI boom. But first, chip giant Nvidia continues to face pressure over its CEO's love affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

item.title: House Republicans consider issuing subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
item.description: Several House Republicans called for a closed-door briefing.

item.title: Asymmetric cyberwarfare: 'States increasingly use cyberattacks in support of their other objectives'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Rafe Pilling, Director of Threat Intelligence in the Sophos Counter Threat Unit (CTU). How can a minor cyber intrusion disrupt food supplies, expose the weaknesses of industrial infrastructure and become an instrument of geopolitical confrontation? The cyberattacks targeting supermarket refrigeration systems in France offer a revealing illustration of how digital vulnerabilities can translate into tangible economic disruption and potentially broader threats to society. As Pilling explains, “With a small amount of effort from the adversary side, they can create a large impact, in this case destroying food and producing empty shelves or empty refrigeration units in stores.” This asymmetry lies at the heart of contemporary cyber conflict, in which modest technical interventions can produce disproportionate economic and operational consequences

item.title: DOJ says Thomas Markle Sr. cut off ankle monitor following arrest
item.description: Markle Sr. was arrested in Florida on one count of possession of child pornography.

item.title: US soldier arrested in Britain on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence
item.description: UK police arrested a senior member of the US Army on Tuesday on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence, adding that the arrest was not related to other counter-terror investigations. The 41-year-old man was detained near the city of Gloucester, west England, and remains in custody.

item.title: What the hack? Europeans face growing psyops and cyberattacks
item.description: So this time, it's Iran, not Russia? France - reportedly acting on US intelligence - summoning Tehran’s ambassador over last month’s hacking of hundreds of supermarket refrigerators that overheated, 15 of which even caught fire. Why now at a time when Iran’s trying to break its international isolation?

item.title: Meghan's father sent to jail after 'cutting off' ankle bracelet
item.description: Thomas Markle has been sent to jail after he allegedly cut off the ankle bracelet monitoring his movements under house arrest.

item.title: Testing the new generation of AI-enabled fire-extinguishing drones
item.description: Drone makers are testing new, big drones that can deliver water or fire retardant with AI assistance. Aspen, Colorado is the first place trying them out. Cool and expensive? Yes. Effective? TBD. (Image credit: Halle Zander)

item.title: U.S. boycotts U.N. human rights review for second year running
item.description: The U.S. has skipped a key U.N. human rights review for the second year running. Rights groups warn the absence risks undermining global accountability. (Image credit: Lian Yi)

item.title: Senior US soldier arrested in UK on allegations of Russia espionage
item.description: A US Army officer has been arrested in the UK over "allegations of espionage" related to Russia, according to British and American officials.

item.title: Ex-investigator admits depriving war crimes probe of potentially valuable information
item.description: A former senior investigating officer for the Royal Military Police has admitted depriving a war crimes investigation of potentially valuable information.

item.title: Filming amongst body bags: New Colombian president’s comms campaign sparks backlash
item.description: Since taking office in August, new far-right Colombian president Abelardo de la Espriella has shared video after video promoting his security forces – especially operations they’ve carried out against armed groups. In some, De la Espriella speaks standing among body bags. Others feature prisoners or look like they were taken from an action film. However, there’s been growing outcry about his social media glorification of repressive policies.

item.title: Train driver 'heard someone screaming' about knifeman stabbing people
item.description: The driver of a London-bound train on which 10 people were stabbed told a court he "heard someone screaming" through a door microphone that a knifeman was attacking people.

item.title: Americans across the economic spectrum feel a 'panic' about finances, author says
item.description: Mona Chalabi spent five years following Americans living paycheck to paycheck, as well as those earning top wages. Her new book, Ten Lives, explores why financial security can feel so elusive. (Image credit: LM Otero)

item.title: French police search Ritz, glitzy Al Fayed properties in women-trafficking probe
item.description: French police have searched several properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, in relation to an investigation into a suspected international network trafficking women for Mohamed Al Fayed, prosecutors told AFP on Tuesday. The Ritz is just one of the late tycoon's high-end ventures where victims have said they faced abuse.

item.title: Iran live updates: Hegseth says Trump 'kicked their teeth in'
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Sports legends whose political fortunes may be a lesson to Riner ahead of presidential bid
item.description: French judo star Teddy Riner may have announced his bid for the 2027 French presidential campaign on Monday, but he is not the only sports star to transition from stadium to bully pulpit. Read about some of his most famous predecessors.

item.title: Seven people taken to hospital after car collides with pedestrians
item.description: Seven people have been taken to hospital after a car collided with a "number of pedestrians" in Glasgow, police say.

item.title: Kristallnacht' 88th anniversary: Merz says Germany faces historic test over antisemitism
item.description: It has been 88 years since "Kristallnacht", the "Night of Broken Glass" in Europe, a violent pogrom against the Jewish population across Nazi Germany and Austria, marking a critical escalation toward the Holocaust. Friedrich Merz, Federal Chancellor of Germany, said that Germany currently faces a historic test over antisemitism.

item.title: US Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth calls impeachment moves 'a farce'
item.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday, November 10, called an effort to impeach him over ​abuse of power in the Iran war a farce and sabotage that plays into the hands of adversaries. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.

item.title: Who exactly is Pete Hegseth, the Pentagon chief facing an impeachment bid?
item.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday dismissed the impeachment effort against him as "a political spectacle". He made the comments a day after Republican Thomas Massie launched a bid to impeach him over his handling of the unpopular war in Iran and other actions. But who is Pete Hegseth? A former Fox News host and military veteran, he has become one of the most prominent figures in the Trump administration.

item.title: French students vow to keep up protest pressure for better learning conditions
item.description: France has been buffeted for months by street protests. They began in September ​with students ‌demanding the renovation of school buildings, more teachers and ⁠university reforms but then turned into broader cost-of-living protests, drawing in trade unions and political activists, and sometimes ‌turning violent.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV visits Argentina in second leg of Latin American tour
item.description: Pope Leo XIV visited Argentina on the second leg of his South American tour, following a stop in Uruguay. During his visit, he celebrated public Masses, met with the faithful and held talks with religious and government leaders. Peru is the final stop on the pontiff's tour.

item.title: REPLAY: US Secretary of State Rubio holds press conference after G7 meeting
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio talked to the press Tuesday as the G7 meets in Paris. He said he saw no need to resume major combat operations against Iran because economic restrictions were working so effectively. He also hailed US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi as "very productive" and said the discussions should be expanded to include Europeans at the table.

item.title: French far right on track to secure €10 million loan for Le Pen's presidential campaign
item.description: France's far-right National Rally party on Tuesday reached a preliminary agreement with two European banks for a loan to help fund Marine Le Pen's presidential campaign. The lenders are expected to finalise the €10 million loan by the end of the month.

item.title: WATCH: What first responders want you to know about surviving rising waters
item.description: ABC News’ Chief Meteorologist Ginger Zee has some eye-opening demonstrations she hopes can help save lives during flash floods.

item.title: UK court overturns Trinidad and Tobago law criminalising homosexual sex
item.description: ‌Trinidad and Tobago's ‌law criminalising consensual sexual ​relations between male same-sex couples has been overturned ‌by a ​UK court.

item.title: REPLAY: Pentagon chief Hegseth holds news briefing amid impeachment push
item.description: US ​Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday called ​moves to impeach him over abuse of power in the Iran war a "farce" that ​would ‌fail. Hegseth made the comment ⁠at a news conference – his first since May – a day after US Representative ‌Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced eight ⁠articles of impeachment against him. Watch our replay.

item.title: G7 talks in Paris try to tackle global crises with uncertainty high over US approach
item.description: Top diplomats from the Group of Seven industrialized democracies gathered in Paris on Monday with clear differences on global crises and questions about how U.S. President Donald Trump will approach foreign policy after his Republican Party’s heavy losses in the midterm elections. Whether on the Russia-Ukraine war, Iran or the International Criminal Court, the sides appeared far apart as two days of talks got underway, as FRANCE 24's Clovis Casali reports.

item.title: ‘It’s a farce’: Hegseth slams impeachment effort
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth dismissed a move to impeach him by a Republican lawmaker as a “farce” and a political “stunt” on Tuesday. It came a day after outgoing US Representative Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth over his handling of the war with Iran and other alleged abuses of power.

item.title: The robot boom: Are businesses ready for an AI-powered workforce?
item.description: As artificial intelligence makes machines more capable and autonomous, businesses are racing to embrace robotics. But while many executives expect to deploy robot fleets in the coming years, far fewer have a clear strategy for doing so. FRANCE 24's Charles Pellegrin speaks to John Healy, Intel's Vice President of Robotics and Industrial Solutions, about the opportunities, risks and workforce challenges behind the growing robot revolution.

item.title: Sophie visits refugee camps on trip to Bangladesh
item.description: Sophie has visited the Rohingya refugee camps at Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh to see the support being offered to displaced people from Myanmar.

item.title: New information from 'several people' about Russell Brand being assessed by police
item.description: Several people have contacted police with allegations and information about Russell Brand during his trial and after it concluded.

item.title: Israel live: Netanyahu bloc targets Arab lawmakers as new parliament is sworn in
item.description: Tensions ran high at the first session of Israel's new parliament on Tuesday as rival camps traded barbs over the possibility of ruling with the support of Arab lists. The party of opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming a government, moved to immediately set up a commission to investigate Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack, an action long resisted by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Follow our live coverage for the latest updates.

item.title: Supreme Court lifts pause on border construction in Big Bend, Texas
item.description: The construction will include physical walls, access roads and vehicle barriers, according to Trump administration plans.

item.title: Gas prices dip below $4 but inflation remains stubbornly high
item.description: Gasoline prices fell below $4 a gallon Tuesday for the first time in three months — but the overall cost of living remains stubbornly high. (Image credit: Ronaldo Schemidt)

item.title: 'Like gods reigning over humans': Many defectors see daughter of North Korea's Kim as heir apparent
item.description: Little is known about her except that she's reportedly about 13 and named Kim Ju Ae, but Korea's spy agency says she's likely her father's heir. (Image credit: 朝鮮通信社)

item.title: 'Clean beauty': How to navigate the latest cosmetic and skincare trends
item.description: It's hard to believe, but Christmas is just six weeks away. That means the battle of the Advent calendars is now well and truly underway. So if you love beauty products but are wanting to buy with safety and a healthy approach in mind, what do you do? Joining us from Atlanta is Lisa Fennessy, the founder and CEO of The New Knew, which reviews "clean beauty" products. She tells us what to look out for to take better care of our skin.

item.title: Indonesia's VP offers resignation as questions mount over his eligibility
item.description: His resignation offer comes amid a widening political rift between Prabowo and Widodo and a separate investigation into allegations that senior police officials wiretapped the president. (Image credit: Dita Alangkara)

item.title: Pokemon's 30-year anniversary: Japanese cards sell like wildfire
item.description: Pokemon, the famous Japanese little monsters, are turning 30, and their trading cards are selling like wildfire, often being flipped for small fortunes. People prepared to camp outside specialised shops in a bid to buy some of these cards.

item.title: The average cost for a new vehicle in the U.S. hits a record high: over $51,000
item.description: Vehicle transaction prices are up to a new record high, according to the Kelley Blue Book — and some buyers are extending their car loans to finance them. (Image credit: Brandon Bell)

item.title: US-mediated talks on ending Russia-Ukraine war begin in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US opened Tuesday, November 10, in the United Arab Emirates, as Washington made another push to end the war. The two-day session in Abu Dhabi is the first such meeting since February. It will focus on establishing future security guarantees for the warring countries.

item.description: Renewed fighting has pushed Ethiopia's healthcare system close to collapse: "The whole emergency (room) was flooded with war trauma patients," one surgeon says of a brutal week in September. (Image credit: AFP)
